items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: I mean Willie Humphrey, who had perhaps a generally thinner tone in the upper register, could project through anything. And he told me a lot about projection

ctx.x: Yeah. And speaking of breathing, it’s like when I listen to this, physically I couldn’t see it but I just felt like you were sucking in all the air in the room to project your sound so that it was very dynamic. And I don’t have a question there, it’s just an observation.

Well you know I’m very much coming out of the traditional New Orleans, the Afro- Creole clarinet tradition. And I got to hear nine players that were born before 1912. And they all had these special unique sounds and tones, and you know I just learned a lot about projection. I mean Willie Humphrey, who had perhaps a generally thinner tone in the upper register, could project through anything. And he told me a lot about projection but also I started out playing in brass bands. I played four years in brass bands in…
How did you learn the repertoire that was required to play the gigs that you just mentioned?
